uncited: They differ from [Distance Color Blending](791-distance-color-blending.md) by relying on geometric normals and reflectance functions rather than volumetric color accumulation, and from [Ray Marching Dither](3269-ray-marching-dither.md) by producing deterministic, non-stochastic results.
They serve as the foundational shading layer for [Diffuse Lighting Models](5343-diffuse-lighting-models.md) and [Specular and Reflective Shading](14299-specular-and-reflective-shading.md).
These models were designed to approximate the appearance of surfaces under local illumination with minimal computational cost, making them suitable for real-time rendering.
In the context of distance-field ray marching, they are adapted to work with implicit geometry where normals are derived from the SDF gradient rather than mesh vertices .
